events.title: Luther posts the Ninety-Five Theses
events.shortBlurb: At Wittenberg an Augustinian friar named Martin Luther set out ninety-five theses against the preaching of indulgences — the spark, by long tradition, of the Protestant Reformation…
body: On 31 October 1517, the vigil of All Saints, Martin Luther, an Augustinian friar and professor of theology at Wittenberg, published ninety-five theses against the preaching of indulgences — by long tradition affixed to the door of the castle church, the university's notice board.

The occasion was the Dominican Johann Tetzel's preaching near Wittenberg of an indulgence toward the rebuilding of St. Peter's in Rome, under a commission whose proceeds were divided between Rome and Archbishop Albert of Mainz. Luther sent the theses to the archbishop; soon translated into German, they were multiplied by the press.

Examined by Cardinal Cajetan at Augsburg in 1518 and pressed by Johann Eck at Leipzig in 1519, Luther came to deny the divine right of the papacy and the inerrancy of councils. The bull Exsurge Domine (1520) condemned forty-one of his propositions; Luther burned it publicly and was excommunicated in January 1521.

Refusing to recant at the Diet of Worms in April 1521, he was sheltered by his prince, Frederick the Wise, at the Wartburg, where he translated the New Testament into German. The revolt divided Western Christendom; the Church answered at the Council of Trent (1545–1563) with reform and definition of doctrine.
